To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the RELOAD and REQUEST instruments have been developed to provide an audit of staff loading and ergonomic aspects of the railway network control room, and that these tools can be used to provide a baseline for the introduction of new technology.

the RELOAD and RESA tools can be used to predict the potential for human error and organizational failure in rail network control operations, that the REQUEST instrument can be used to audit the ergonomics aspects in railway control operations, and that the workshop approach can be used to develop an understanding of the roles and responsibilities of the different staff groups in rail network control.
The RELOAD tool can be used to identify the most demanding tasks for signallers and electrical controllers, and that these are often associated with the management of complex and changing situations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of ergonomics to the design, development and operation of railway network control systems.
the application of ergonomics principles to the assessment of railway network control operations.
the application of ergonomics in the context of railway network operations and the development of tools to assess and improve the quality of work and working conditions.

the RELOAD tool is the best of the RECAP tools, and the REQUEST tool the least successful.
ergonomics in rail operations is on the right track.
ergonomics is a key element to the successful implementation of new railway control systems and the development of new working practices.

we are on the right track with RECAP, but we need to develop a wider perspective of the railway network control environment.
we have developed a range of tools for the assessment of the ergonomic aspects of rail network control.

the ergonomics of railway network operations is a rich and challenging field for cognitive ergonomics research.
the RECAP tools have been successfully used in the field and that the tools are robust enough to be applied in other railway networks.
ergonomics can be systematically applied across the railway network, and that this can be done with relatively little cost.
